A little about our guitarist...
Joey is a 15 year old guitarist who began taking lessons on his 8th birthday. However, his love for music started much earlier. His very first guitar performance was at the age of 9 in front of over 200 people at his school concert. He alone performed AC/DC’s Back in Black. The response from the crowd confirmed that this was a path he wanted for his future. At the age of 13, Joey began taking piano lessons and excelled very quickly. He has been active in his school jazz band since the 5th grade playing guitar and has been known to step in and lend support on bass whenever needed. His efforts were recognized with awards he received. Joey also participated in a school play by providing and creating the background music through its entirety.
In his spare time, Joey started volunteering his piano and guitar talents at a local senior center where his great grandmother stayed for a short time. Music is something that connects people of all ages and this casual setting is very rewarding to both Joey and the seniors. It has been such an uplifting experience that more senior centers are reaching out to Joey to play.

**Steven Siro Vai**[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-fullname-2) ( _VYE_; born June 6, 1960) is an American guitarist, songwriter, and producer. A three-time Grammy Award winner and fifteen-time nominee,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-tecawards.org-3) Vai started his music career in 1978 at the age of eighteen as a transcriptionist for Frank Zappa,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-Tempo_Mental-4) and played in Zappa's band from 1980 to 1983.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-tecawards.org-3) He embarked on a solo career in 1983 and has released 11 solo albums to date.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-5) He has recorded and toured with Alcatrazz, David Lee Roth, and Whitesnake, as well as recording with artists such as Ozzy Osbourne, Public Image Ltd, Mary J. Blige, Spinal Tap, Alice Cooper, Motörhead, and Polyphia. Additionally, Vai has toured with live-only acts G3, Zappa Plays Zappa, Beat (playing 1980s era King Crimson) and the Experience Hendrix Tour, as well as headlining international tours.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-VAI_Bands-6)

Vai has been described as a "highly individualistic player" and part of a generation of "heavy rock and metal virtuosi who came to the fore in the 1980s".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-7) He released his first solo album _Flex-Able_ in 1984, while his most successful release, _Passion and Warfare_ (1990), was described as "the richest and best hard rock guitar-virtuoso album of the '80s".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-AllmusicPW-8) He was voted the "10th Greatest Guitarist" by _Guitar World_ magazine's readers,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-guitarworld.com-9) and has sold over 15 million records.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-tecawards.org-3)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-10)
Steve Vai in 2017

Steve Vai, a descendant of Italian immigrants, was born in Carle Place, New York on June 6, 1960. He is the fourth son of John and Theresa Vai.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-11) Vai was raised Roman Catholic.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-12) He described his first experiences with music as, "at the age of five I walked up to [a] piano, hit a note, and noticed that to the right the notes go higher and to the left the notes go lower. In that very moment, I had a full-on epiphany. I was flooded with the instinctual realization of how music was created and how it worked from a theoretical standpoint—the whole language of music was very obvious. I also understood immediately, instinctually, and unequivocally something that has only deepened through the years: that the creation of music is an infinite personal expression. I realized that I could do this, I could make music, and it could be whatever I want."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-http://facebook.com/MakeWeirdMusic-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-americansongwriter.com-15)
It was a year later, at the age of six, that Vai experienced his introduction to the guitar, remembering that, "I saw this nine-year-old boy playing the guitar in my grade school auditorium, and that was another epiphany that I had. It was my first recognition of the instrument. When I saw that guitar and I saw this kid playing it, I knew instinctually that I was going to play the guitar someday, and that it would be my instrument. Don't ask me how I knew, I just knew. It was the coolest thing I had ever seen."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-http://facebook.com/MakeWeirdMusic-13)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-americansongwriter.com-15)

As a young child, Vai was influenced by the music his parents had listened to. The album that he cites as his "musical awakening" was the original motion picture soundtrack to the 1961 film _West Side Story_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-16) At age eleven, Vai was introduced to the contemporary rock and progressive music of the era, and after hearing the guitar solo to Led Zeppelin's "Heartbreaker" at age twelve, decided to begin playing the guitar.
In 1973, Vai began to take guitar lessons from fellow New York native Joe Satriani, and played in local bands (the Ohio Express, Circus, and Rayge) throughout his high school years.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-10_Things-17) His friend John Sergio gave him Joe Satriani's number so that Steve and his friend Frankie Munn could get guitar lessons.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-19) In 1978, to further pursue his interest in music composition and theory, Vai attended Berklee College of Music in Boston, Massachusetts after graduating from Carle Place High School.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-20) While at Berklee, Vai began working for Frank Zappa as a transcriptionist, and in the middle of his fourth semester, moved to California to start his career as a session and touring artist for Zappa.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-BerkleePress-21) Also while at Berklee, Vai met his future spouse Pia Maiocco. They have been together since they met and have two children.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-imdbPia-22) In 2003, Vai was awarded an Honorary Doctorate of Music from Berklee.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-23)

### Early music career (1978–1986)
[edit]
Steve Vai (on guitar in between the drums and keyboard, to the right), Frank Zappa and band during a concert at the Memorial Auditorium in Buffalo, New York (October 25, 1980)
In 1978, Vai sent both a notated transcription of Frank Zappa's "The Black Page", and a recording of his college band, Morning Thunder, to Zappa.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-BerkleePress-21)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-VaiVideo-24) Impressed by this, Zappa responded by putting Vai on salary to transcribe his work, which included pieces from the _[Joe's Garage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe's\_Garage "Joe's Garage")_ and _[Shut Up 'n Play Yer Guitar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shut\_Up\_'n\_Play\_Yer\_Guitar "Shut Up 'n Play Yer Guitar")_ albums.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-Tempo_Mental-4) After leaving Berklee College of Music and moving to California, Vai auditioned[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-25) for and became a full-time member of Zappa's band, going on his first tour with Zappa in late 1980.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-BerkleePress-21) Zappa often referred to Vai as his "little Italian virtuoso",[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-26) and Vai is frequently listed in the liner notes of Zappa's albums as having performed "stunt" or "impossible" guitar parts.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-Play_Like_Steve_Vai-27)

### Early music career (1978–1986)
Vai was a featured artist on the 1993 release _[Zappa's Universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zappa's\_Universe "Zappa's Universe")_, and in 2006, Vai appeared as a special guest on Dweezil Zappa's Zappa Plays Zappa tour; both projects won Vai a Grammy Award.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-VaiAwards-28)
After moving on from Zappa's employ in 1983, Vai bought a house in Sylmar, Los Angeles, where he built his first professional studio.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-VaiStudios-29) During this period, Vai formed two bands (The Classified and 777)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-VAI_Bands-6) as well as writing and recording a large amount of music that was not originally intended for release. Out of this material, Vai compiled his first studio album _Flex-Able_. He created his own record label, Akashic Records (later Light Without Heat Records), which he used to take _Flex-Able_ directly to distribution channels.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-30)_Flex-Able_ was released in January 1984.

### Early music career (1978–1986)
Vai began his rise to public acclaim in 1983 when, shortly before the release of _Flex-Able_, his composition "The Attitude Song" was published in _Guitar Player_ magazine.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-Play_Like_Steve_Vai-27) The song centered itself on a main guitar riff in the time signature 7/16, played over a rhythm section centered in 4/4. Each following section of the song showcased a number of specialized techniques (such as two-handed tapping, whammy bar acrobatics, sweep picking, alternate picking, multi-part harmonies, and odd phrasing) used in angular and exaggerated ways that were unique to the song at the time.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-Play_Like_Steve_Vai-27) Interest from the public grew even greater when Vai's song "Blue Powder" (a demonstration for the Carvin X100b amplifier) was published in _Guitar Player_ as well, which showed the virtuoso side of Vai's compositional process. Also in 1986, Vai was cast in the film _Crossroads_ as the Devil's guitar player "Jack Butler". In the famous "duel scene" between Vai and Ralph Macchio's character, Vai wrote and performed all guitar parts with the exception of the slide guitar, which was performed by Ry Cooder.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-31)
In between solo work, Vai replaced Yngwie Malmsteen in June 1984 as the lead guitarist of Alcatrazz, with whom he recorded the album _Disturbing the Peace_. Vai left shortly after the subsequent tour to join David Lee Roth's band.

Well, the youngest (meaning any member) would be The Jackson 5. They were signed onto Motown Records in 1968 when Michael Jackson was only 9 years old. Marlon was 10, Jermaine was 13, Tito was 14, and Jackie was 17. In the next several years with Motown, The Jackson 5 were absolutely huge with more than a dozen top-40 hits, millions of records sold, and many national TV appearances. Michael even started releasing his first solo work. And the rest is history.
The other band that comes to mind is Hanson, which is best known for their 1997 mega-hit “MMMBop.” To date, they’ve sold around 16 million albums and had three top-20 albums and three top-20 singles (“MMMBop” hit #1). At the time of “MMMBop” the three Hanson brothers were 16, 14, and 11 years old.
Menudo — the Latin boy band from the 1980s — was huge as well, but none of the members were as young as Michael Jackson, Marlon Jackson, or Zac Hanson when they hit success. At the time Menudo hit international fame with their 1981 album Quiero Ser, the five boys were ages 13 and 14. (Incidentally, this did not include their most famous member — Ricky Martin — who wasn’t a part of the group until 1984.)

texts.1: **Steven Siro Vai**[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-fullname-2) ( _VYE_; born June 6, 1960) is an American guitarist, songwriter, and producer. A three-time Grammy Award winner and fifteen-time nominee,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-tecawards.org-3) Vai started his music career in 1978 at the age of eighteen as a transcriptionist for Frank Zappa,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-Tempo_Mental-4) and played in Zappa's band from 1980 to 1983.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-tecawards.org-3) He embarked on a solo career in 1983 and has released 11 solo albums to date.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-5) He has recorded and toured with Alcatrazz, David Lee Roth, and Whitesnake, as well as recording with artists such as Ozzy Osbourne, Public Image Ltd, Mary J. Blige, Spinal Tap, Alice Cooper, Motörhead, and Polyphia. Additionally, Vai has toured with live-only acts G3, Zappa Plays Zappa, Beat (playing 1980s era King Crimson) and the Experience Hendrix Tour, as well as headlining international tours.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-VAI_Bands-6)
texts.2:
Vai has been described as a "highly individualistic player" and part of a generation of "heavy rock and metal virtuosi who came to the fore in the 1980s".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-7) He released his first solo album _Flex-Able_ in 1984, while his most successful release, _Passion and Warfare_ (1990), was described as "the richest and best hard rock guitar-virtuoso album of the '80s".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-AllmusicPW-8) He was voted the "10th Greatest Guitarist" by _Guitar World_ magazine's readers,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-guitarworld.com-9) and has sold over 15 million records.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-tecawards.org-3)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-10)
Steve Vai in 2017
texts.3:
Steve Vai, a descendant of Italian immigrants, was born in Carle Place, New York on June 6, 1960. He is the fourth son of John and Theresa Vai.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-11) Vai was raised Roman Catholic.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-12) He described his first experiences with music as, "at the age of five I walked up to [a] piano, hit a note, and noticed that to the right the notes go higher and to the left the notes go lower. In that very moment, I had a full-on epiphany. I was flooded with the instinctual realization of how music was created and how it worked from a theoretical standpoint—the whole language of music was very obvious. I also understood immediately, instinctually, and unequivocally something that has only deepened through the years: that the creation of music is an infinite personal expression. I realized that I could do this, I could make music, and it could be whatever I want."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-http://facebook.com/MakeWeirdMusic-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-americansongwriter.com-15)
It was a year later, at the age of six, that Vai experienced his introduction to the guitar, remembering that, "I saw this nine-year-old boy playing the guitar in my grade school auditorium, and that was another epiphany that I had. It was my first recognition of the instrument. When I saw that guitar and I saw this kid playing it, I knew instinctually that I was going to play the guitar someday, and that it would be my instrument. Don't ask me how I knew, I just knew. It was the coolest thing I had ever seen."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-http://facebook.com/MakeWeirdMusic-13)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-americansongwriter.com-15)
texts.4:
As a young child, Vai was influenced by the music his parents had listened to. The album that he cites as his "musical awakening" was the original motion picture soundtrack to the 1961 film _West Side Story_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-16) At age eleven, Vai was introduced to the contemporary rock and progressive music of the era, and after hearing the guitar solo to Led Zeppelin's "Heartbreaker" at age twelve, decided to begin playing the guitar.
In 1973, Vai began to take guitar lessons from fellow New York native Joe Satriani, and played in local bands (the Ohio Express, Circus, and Rayge) throughout his high school years.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-10_Things-17) His friend John Sergio gave him Joe Satriani's number so that Steve and his friend Frankie Munn could get guitar lessons.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-19) In 1978, to further pursue his interest in music composition and theory, Vai attended Berklee College of Music in Boston, Massachusetts after graduating from Carle Place High School.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-20) While at Berklee, Vai began working for Frank Zappa as a transcriptionist, and in the middle of his fourth semester, moved to California to start his career as a session and touring artist for Zappa.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-BerkleePress-21) Also while at Berklee, Vai met his future spouse Pia Maiocco. They have been together since they met and have two children.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-imdbPia-22) In 2003, Vai was awarded an Honorary Doctorate of Music from Berklee.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-23)
texts.5:
### Early music career (1978–1986)
[edit]
Steve Vai (on guitar in between the drums and keyboard, to the right), Frank Zappa and band during a concert at the Memorial Auditorium in Buffalo, New York (October 25, 1980)
In 1978, Vai sent both a notated transcription of Frank Zappa's "The Black Page", and a recording of his college band, Morning Thunder, to Zappa.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-BerkleePress-21)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-VaiVideo-24) Impressed by this, Zappa responded by putting Vai on salary to transcribe his work, which included pieces from the _[Joe's Garage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe's\_Garage "Joe's Garage")_ and _[Shut Up 'n Play Yer Guitar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shut\_Up\_'n\_Play\_Yer\_Guitar "Shut Up 'n Play Yer Guitar")_ albums.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-Tempo_Mental-4) After leaving Berklee College of Music and moving to California, Vai auditioned[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-25) for and became a full-time member of Zappa's band, going on his first tour with Zappa in late 1980.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-BerkleePress-21) Zappa often referred to Vai as his "little Italian virtuoso",[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-26) and Vai is frequently listed in the liner notes of Zappa's albums as having performed "stunt" or "impossible" guitar parts.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-Play_Like_Steve_Vai-27)
texts.6:
### Early music career (1978–1986)
Vai was a featured artist on the 1993 release _[Zappa's Universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zappa's\_Universe "Zappa's Universe")_, and in 2006, Vai appeared as a special guest on Dweezil Zappa's Zappa Plays Zappa tour; both projects won Vai a Grammy Award.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-VaiAwards-28)
After moving on from Zappa's employ in 1983, Vai bought a house in Sylmar, Los Angeles, where he built his first professional studio.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-VaiStudios-29) During this period, Vai formed two bands (The Classified and 777)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-VAI_Bands-6) as well as writing and recording a large amount of music that was not originally intended for release. Out of this material, Vai compiled his first studio album _Flex-Able_. He created his own record label, Akashic Records (later Light Without Heat Records), which he used to take _Flex-Able_ directly to distribution channels.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-30)_Flex-Able_ was released in January 1984.
texts.7:
### Early music career (1978–1986)
Vai began his rise to public acclaim in 1983 when, shortly before the release of _Flex-Able_, his composition "The Attitude Song" was published in _Guitar Player_ magazine.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-Play_Like_Steve_Vai-27) The song centered itself on a main guitar riff in the time signature 7/16, played over a rhythm section centered in 4/4. Each following section of the song showcased a number of specialized techniques (such as two-handed tapping, whammy bar acrobatics, sweep picking, alternate picking, multi-part harmonies, and odd phrasing) used in angular and exaggerated ways that were unique to the song at the time.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-Play_Like_Steve_Vai-27) Interest from the public grew even greater when Vai's song "Blue Powder" (a demonstration for the Carvin X100b amplifier) was published in _Guitar Player_ as well, which showed the virtuoso side of Vai's compositional process. Also in 1986, Vai was cast in the film _Crossroads_ as the Devil's guitar player "Jack Butler". In the famous "duel scene" between Vai and Ralph Macchio's character, Vai wrote and performed all guitar parts with the exception of the slide guitar, which was performed by Ry Cooder.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-31)
In between solo work, Vai replaced Yngwie Malmsteen in June 1984 as the lead guitarist of Alcatrazz, with whom he recorded the album _Disturbing the Peace_. Vai left shortly after the subsequent tour to join David Lee Roth's band.

A little about our guitarist...
Joey is a 15 year old guitarist who began taking lessons on his 8th birthday. However, his love for music started much earlier. His very first guitar performance was at the age of 9 in front of over 200 people at his school concert. He alone performed AC/DC’s Back in Black. The response from the crowd confirmed that this was a path he wanted for his future. At the age of 13, Joey began taking piano lessons and excelled very quickly. He has been active in his school jazz band since the 5th grade playing guitar and has been known to step in and lend support on bass whenever needed. His efforts were recognized with awards he received. Joey also participated in a school play by providing and creating the background music through its entirety.
In his spare time, Joey started volunteering his piano and guitar talents at a local senior center where his great grandmother stayed for a short time. Music is something that connects people of all ages and this casual setting is very rewarding to both Joey and the seniors. It has been such an uplifting experience that more senior centers are reaching out to Joey to play.

**Steven Siro Vai**[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-fullname-2) ( _VYE_; born June 6, 1960) is an American guitarist, songwriter, and producer. A three-time Grammy Award winner and fifteen-time nominee,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-tecawards.org-3) Vai started his music career in 1978 at the age of eighteen as a transcriptionist for Frank Zappa,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-Tempo_Mental-4) and played in Zappa's band from 1980 to 1983.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-tecawards.org-3) He embarked on a solo career in 1983 and has released 11 solo albums to date.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-5) He has recorded and toured with Alcatrazz, David Lee Roth, and Whitesnake, as well as recording with artists such as Ozzy Osbourne, Public Image Ltd, Mary J. Blige, Spinal Tap, Alice Cooper, Motörhead, and Polyphia. Additionally, Vai has toured with live-only acts G3, Zappa Plays Zappa, Beat (playing 1980s era King Crimson) and the Experience Hendrix Tour, as well as headlining international tours.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-VAI_Bands-6)

Vai has been described as a "highly individualistic player" and part of a generation of "heavy rock and metal virtuosi who came to the fore in the 1980s".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-7) He released his first solo album _Flex-Able_ in 1984, while his most successful release, _Passion and Warfare_ (1990), was described as "the richest and best hard rock guitar-virtuoso album of the '80s".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-AllmusicPW-8) He was voted the "10th Greatest Guitarist" by _Guitar World_ magazine's readers,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-guitarworld.com-9) and has sold over 15 million records.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-tecawards.org-3)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-10)
Steve Vai in 2017

Steve Vai, a descendant of Italian immigrants, was born in Carle Place, New York on June 6, 1960. He is the fourth son of John and Theresa Vai.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-11) Vai was raised Roman Catholic.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-12) He described his first experiences with music as, "at the age of five I walked up to [a] piano, hit a note, and noticed that to the right the notes go higher and to the left the notes go lower. In that very moment, I had a full-on epiphany. I was flooded with the instinctual realization of how music was created and how it worked from a theoretical standpoint—the whole language of music was very obvious. I also understood immediately, instinctually, and unequivocally something that has only deepened through the years: that the creation of music is an infinite personal expression. I realized that I could do this, I could make music, and it could be whatever I want."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-http://facebook.com/MakeWeirdMusic-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-americansongwriter.com-15)
It was a year later, at the age of six, that Vai experienced his introduction to the guitar, remembering that, "I saw this nine-year-old boy playing the guitar in my grade school auditorium, and that was another epiphany that I had. It was my first recognition of the instrument. When I saw that guitar and I saw this kid playing it, I knew instinctually that I was going to play the guitar someday, and that it would be my instrument. Don't ask me how I knew, I just knew. It was the coolest thing I had ever seen."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-http://facebook.com/MakeWeirdMusic-13)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-americansongwriter.com-15)

As a young child, Vai was influenced by the music his parents had listened to. The album that he cites as his "musical awakening" was the original motion picture soundtrack to the 1961 film _West Side Story_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-16) At age eleven, Vai was introduced to the contemporary rock and progressive music of the era, and after hearing the guitar solo to Led Zeppelin's "Heartbreaker" at age twelve, decided to begin playing the guitar.
In 1973, Vai began to take guitar lessons from fellow New York native Joe Satriani, and played in local bands (the Ohio Express, Circus, and Rayge) throughout his high school years.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-10_Things-17) His friend John Sergio gave him Joe Satriani's number so that Steve and his friend Frankie Munn could get guitar lessons.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-19) In 1978, to further pursue his interest in music composition and theory, Vai attended Berklee College of Music in Boston, Massachusetts after graduating from Carle Place High School.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-20) While at Berklee, Vai began working for Frank Zappa as a transcriptionist, and in the middle of his fourth semester, moved to California to start his career as a session and touring artist for Zappa.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-BerkleePress-21) Also while at Berklee, Vai met his future spouse Pia Maiocco. They have been together since they met and have two children.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-imdbPia-22) In 2003, Vai was awarded an Honorary Doctorate of Music from Berklee.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-23)

### Early music career (1978–1986)
[edit]
Steve Vai (on guitar in between the drums and keyboard, to the right), Frank Zappa and band during a concert at the Memorial Auditorium in Buffalo, New York (October 25, 1980)
In 1978, Vai sent both a notated transcription of Frank Zappa's "The Black Page", and a recording of his college band, Morning Thunder, to Zappa.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-BerkleePress-21)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-VaiVideo-24) Impressed by this, Zappa responded by putting Vai on salary to transcribe his work, which included pieces from the _[Joe's Garage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe's\_Garage "Joe's Garage")_ and _[Shut Up 'n Play Yer Guitar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shut\_Up\_'n\_Play\_Yer\_Guitar "Shut Up 'n Play Yer Guitar")_ albums.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-Tempo_Mental-4) After leaving Berklee College of Music and moving to California, Vai auditioned[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-25) for and became a full-time member of Zappa's band, going on his first tour with Zappa in late 1980.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-BerkleePress-21) Zappa often referred to Vai as his "little Italian virtuoso",[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-26) and Vai is frequently listed in the liner notes of Zappa's albums as having performed "stunt" or "impossible" guitar parts.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-Play_Like_Steve_Vai-27)

### Early music career (1978–1986)
Vai was a featured artist on the 1993 release _[Zappa's Universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zappa's\_Universe "Zappa's Universe")_, and in 2006, Vai appeared as a special guest on Dweezil Zappa's Zappa Plays Zappa tour; both projects won Vai a Grammy Award.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-VaiAwards-28)
After moving on from Zappa's employ in 1983, Vai bought a house in Sylmar, Los Angeles, where he built his first professional studio.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-VaiStudios-29) During this period, Vai formed two bands (The Classified and 777)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-VAI_Bands-6) as well as writing and recording a large amount of music that was not originally intended for release. Out of this material, Vai compiled his first studio album _Flex-Able_. He created his own record label, Akashic Records (later Light Without Heat Records), which he used to take _Flex-Able_ directly to distribution channels.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-30)_Flex-Able_ was released in January 1984.

### Early music career (1978–1986)
Vai began his rise to public acclaim in 1983 when, shortly before the release of _Flex-Able_, his composition "The Attitude Song" was published in _Guitar Player_ magazine.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-Play_Like_Steve_Vai-27) The song centered itself on a main guitar riff in the time signature 7/16, played over a rhythm section centered in 4/4. Each following section of the song showcased a number of specialized techniques (such as two-handed tapping, whammy bar acrobatics, sweep picking, alternate picking, multi-part harmonies, and odd phrasing) used in angular and exaggerated ways that were unique to the song at the time.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-Play_Like_Steve_Vai-27) Interest from the public grew even greater when Vai's song "Blue Powder" (a demonstration for the Carvin X100b amplifier) was published in _Guitar Player_ as well, which showed the virtuoso side of Vai's compositional process. Also in 1986, Vai was cast in the film _Crossroads_ as the Devil's guitar player "Jack Butler". In the famous "duel scene" between Vai and Ralph Macchio's character, Vai wrote and performed all guitar parts with the exception of the slide guitar, which was performed by Ry Cooder.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-31)
In between solo work, Vai replaced Yngwie Malmsteen in June 1984 as the lead guitarist of Alcatrazz, with whom he recorded the album _Disturbing the Peace_. Vai left shortly after the subsequent tour to join David Lee Roth's band.

A little about our guitarist...
Joey is a 15 year old guitarist who began taking lessons on his 8th birthday. However, his love for music started much earlier. His very first guitar performance was at the age of 9 in front of over 200 people at his school concert. He alone performed AC/DC’s Back in Black. The response from the crowd confirmed that this was a path he wanted for his future. At the age of 13, Joey began taking piano lessons and excelled very quickly. He has been active in his school jazz band since the 5th grade playing guitar and has been known to step in and lend support on bass whenever needed. His efforts were recognized with awards he received. Joey also participated in a school play by providing and creating the background music through its entirety.
In his spare time, Joey started volunteering his piano and guitar talents at a local senior center where his great grandmother stayed for a short time. Music is something that connects people of all ages and this casual setting is very rewarding to both Joey and the seniors. It has been such an uplifting experience that more senior centers are reaching out to Joey to play.

Well, the youngest (meaning any member) would be The Jackson 5. They were signed onto Motown Records in 1968 when Michael Jackson was only 9 years old. **Steven Siro Vai**[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-fullname-2) ( _VYE_; born June 6, 1960) is an American guitarist, songwriter, and producer. A three-time Grammy Award winner and fifteen-time nominee,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-tecawards.org-3) Vai started his music career in 1978 at the age of eighteen as a transcriptionist for Frank Zappa,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-Tempo_Mental-4) and played in Zappa's band from 1980 to 1983.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-tecawards.org-3) He embarked on a solo career in 1983 and has released 11 solo albums to date.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-5) He has recorded and toured with Alcatrazz, David Lee Roth, and Whitesnake, as well as recording with artists such as Ozzy Osbourne, Public Image Ltd, Mary J. Blige, Spinal Tap, Alice Cooper, Motörhead, and Polyphia. Additionally, Vai has toured with live-only acts G3, Zappa Plays Zappa, Beat (playing 1980s era King Crimson) and the Experience Hendrix Tour, as well as headlining international tours.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-VAI_Bands-6)

Vai has been described as a "highly individualistic player" and part of a generation of "heavy rock and metal virtuosi who came to the fore in the 1980s".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-7) He released his first solo album _Flex-Able_ in 1984, while his most successful release, _Passion and Warfare_ (1990), was described as "the richest and best hard rock guitar-virtuoso album of the '80s".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-AllmusicPW-8) He was voted the "10th Greatest Guitarist" by _Guitar World_ magazine's readers,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-guitarworld.com-9) and has sold over 15 million records.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-tecawards.org-3)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-10)
Steve Vai in 2017

Steve Vai, a descendant of Italian immigrants, was born in Carle Place, New York on June 6, 1960. He is the fourth son of John and Theresa Vai.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-11) Vai was raised Roman Catholic.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-12) He described his first experiences with music as, "at the age of five I walked up to [a] piano, hit a note, and noticed that to the right the notes go higher and to the left the notes go lower. In that very moment, I had a full-on epiphany. I was flooded with the instinctual realization of how music was created and how it worked from a theoretical standpoint—the whole language of music was very obvious. I also understood immediately, instinctually, and unequivocally something that has only deepened through the years: that the creation of music is an infinite personal expression. I realized that I could do this, I could make music, and it could be whatever I want."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-http://facebook.com/MakeWeirdMusic-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-americansongwriter.com-15)
It was a year later, at the age of six, that Vai experienced his introduction to the guitar, remembering that, "I saw this nine-year-old boy playing the guitar in my grade school auditorium, and that was another epiphany that I had. It was my first recognition of the instrument. When I saw that guitar and I saw this kid playing it, I knew instinctually that I was going to play the guitar someday, and that it would be my instrument. Don't ask me how I knew, I just knew. It was the coolest thing I had ever seen."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-http://facebook.com/MakeWeirdMusic-13)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-americansongwriter.com-15)

As a young child, Vai was influenced by the music his parents had listened to. The album that he cites as his "musical awakening" was the original motion picture soundtrack to the 1961 film _West Side Story_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-16) At age eleven, Vai was introduced to the contemporary rock and progressive music of the era, and after hearing the guitar solo to Led Zeppelin's "Heartbreaker" at age twelve, decided to begin playing the guitar.
In 1973, Vai began to take guitar lessons from fellow New York native Joe Satriani, and played in local bands (the Ohio Express, Circus, and Rayge) throughout his high school years.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-10_Things-17) His friend John Sergio gave him Joe Satriani's number so that Steve and his friend Frankie Munn could get guitar lessons.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-19) In 1978, to further pursue his interest in music composition and theory, Vai attended Berklee College of Music in Boston, Massachusetts after graduating from Carle Place High School.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-20) While at Berklee, Vai began working for Frank Zappa as a transcriptionist, and in the middle of his fourth semester, moved to California to start his career as a session and touring artist for Zappa.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-BerkleePress-21) Also while at Berklee, Vai met his future spouse Pia Maiocco. They have been together since they met and have two children.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-imdbPia-22) In 2003, Vai was awarded an Honorary Doctorate of Music from Berklee.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-23)

### Early music career (1978–1986)
[edit]
Steve Vai (on guitar in between the drums and keyboard, to the right), Frank Zappa and band during a concert at the Memorial Auditorium in Buffalo, New York (October 25, 1980)
In 1978, Vai sent both a notated transcription of Frank Zappa's "The Black Page", and a recording of his college band, Morning Thunder, to Zappa.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-BerkleePress-21)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-VaiVideo-24) Impressed by this, Zappa responded by putting Vai on salary to transcribe his work, which included pieces from the _[Joe's Garage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe's\_Garage "Joe's Garage")_ and _[Shut Up 'n Play Yer Guitar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shut\_Up\_'n\_Play\_Yer\_Guitar "Shut Up 'n Play Yer Guitar")_ albums.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-Tempo_Mental-4) After leaving Berklee College of Music and moving to California, Vai auditioned[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-25) for and became a full-time member of Zappa's band, going on his first tour with Zappa in late 1980.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-BerkleePress-21) Zappa often referred to Vai as his "little Italian virtuoso",[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-26) and Vai is frequently listed in the liner notes of Zappa's albums as having performed "stunt" or "impossible" guitar parts.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-Play_Like_Steve_Vai-27)

### Early music career (1978–1986)
Vai was a featured artist on the 1993 release _[Zappa's Universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zappa's\_Universe "Zappa's Universe")_, and in 2006, Vai appeared as a special guest on Dweezil Zappa's Zappa Plays Zappa tour; both projects won Vai a Grammy Award.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-VaiAwards-28)
After moving on from Zappa's employ in 1983, Vai bought a house in Sylmar, Los Angeles, where he built his first professional studio.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-VaiStudios-29) During this period, Vai formed two bands (The Classified and 777)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-VAI_Bands-6) as well as writing and recording a large amount of music that was not originally intended for release. Out of this material, Vai compiled his first studio album _Flex-Able_. He created his own record label, Akashic Records (later Light Without Heat Records), which he used to take _Flex-Able_ directly to distribution channels.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-30)_Flex-Able_ was released in January 1984.

### Early music career (1978–1986)
Vai began his rise to public acclaim in 1983 when, shortly before the release of _Flex-Able_, his composition "The Attitude Song" was published in _Guitar Player_ magazine.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-Play_Like_Steve_Vai-27) The song centered itself on a main guitar riff in the time signature 7/16, played over a rhythm section centered in 4/4. Each following section of the song showcased a number of specialized techniques (such as two-handed tapping, whammy bar acrobatics, sweep picking, alternate picking, multi-part harmonies, and odd phrasing) used in angular and exaggerated ways that were unique to the song at the time.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-Play_Like_Steve_Vai-27) Interest from the public grew even greater when Vai's song "Blue Powder" (a demonstration for the Carvin X100b amplifier) was published in _Guitar Player_ as well, which showed the virtuoso side of Vai's compositional process. Also in 1986, Vai was cast in the film _Crossroads_ as the Devil's guitar player "Jack Butler". In the famous "duel scene" between Vai and Ralph Macchio's character, Vai wrote and performed all guitar parts with the exception of the slide guitar, which was performed by Ry Cooder.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-31)
In between solo work, Vai replaced Yngwie Malmsteen in June 1984 as the lead guitarist of Alcatrazz, with whom he recorded the album _Disturbing the Peace_. Vai left shortly after the subsequent tour to join David Lee Roth's band.

While I was attending [Berklee College of Music](https://www.facebook.com/BerkleeCollege?__cft__[0]=AZiSYXVnITcak-NXqcgIPsnrNloK2y8ho5uUJJUQmtU6zXXQECJJ0Y_DKxVGffhiY9szQ5WHTXOpf2d6qNxn4s9b5DK_FEMLOkmYgp1ciRarqnWYsztnzVLivjGh5gWdQA8zaK-Zh4P-8BpsrmEi-VcfNSelmXSQSQ&__tn__=-]K-R) in 1978-79, I was in various bands with some outrageously talented young musicians. The first band I formed with my friend Dave Rosenthal was called “Morning Thunder”. Great name for a group ay?
We used to write intense and complex fusion type music with a twist. The band was very bonded and we played with some unbridled youthful chops and insanity.
The band was:
Steve Vai - Guitar
Randy Coven - Bass
Dave Rosenthal - Keyboards
Eddie Rogers - Drums

texts.1: **Steven Siro Vai**[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-fullname-2) ( _VYE_; born June 6, 1960) is an American guitarist, songwriter, and producer. A three-time Grammy Award winner and fifteen-time nominee,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-tecawards.org-3) Vai started his music career in 1978 at the age of eighteen as a transcriptionist for Frank Zappa,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-Tempo_Mental-4) and played in Zappa's band from 1980 to 1983.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-tecawards.org-3) He embarked on a solo career in 1983 and has released 11 solo albums to date.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-5) He has recorded and toured with Alcatrazz, David Lee Roth, and Whitesnake, as well as recording with artists such as Ozzy Osbourne, Public Image Ltd, Mary J. Blige, Spinal Tap, Alice Cooper, Motörhead, and Polyphia. Additionally, Vai has toured with live-only acts G3, Zappa Plays Zappa, Beat (playing 1980s era King Crimson) and the Experience Hendrix Tour, as well as headlining international tours.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-VAI_Bands-6)
texts.2:
Vai has been described as a "highly individualistic player" and part of a generation of "heavy rock and metal virtuosi who came to the fore in the 1980s".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-7) He released his first solo album _Flex-Able_ in 1984, while his most successful release, _Passion and Warfare_ (1990), was described as "the richest and best hard rock guitar-virtuoso album of the '80s".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-AllmusicPW-8) He was voted the "10th Greatest Guitarist" by _Guitar World_ magazine's readers,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-guitarworld.com-9) and has sold over 15 million records.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-tecawards.org-3)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-10)
Steve Vai in 2017
texts.3:
Steve Vai, a descendant of Italian immigrants, was born in Carle Place, New York on June 6, 1960. He is the fourth son of John and Theresa Vai.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-11) Vai was raised Roman Catholic.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-12) He described his first experiences with music as, "at the age of five I walked up to [a] piano, hit a note, and noticed that to the right the notes go higher and to the left the notes go lower. In that very moment, I had a full-on epiphany. I was flooded with the instinctual realization of how music was created and how it worked from a theoretical standpoint—the whole language of music was very obvious. I also understood immediately, instinctually, and unequivocally something that has only deepened through the years: that the creation of music is an infinite personal expression. I realized that I could do this, I could make music, and it could be whatever I want."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-http://facebook.com/MakeWeirdMusic-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-americansongwriter.com-15)
It was a year later, at the age of six, that Vai experienced his introduction to the guitar, remembering that, "I saw this nine-year-old boy playing the guitar in my grade school auditorium, and that was another epiphany that I had. It was my first recognition of the instrument. When I saw that guitar and I saw this kid playing it, I knew instinctually that I was going to play the guitar someday, and that it would be my instrument. Don't ask me how I knew, I just knew. It was the coolest thing I had ever seen."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-http://facebook.com/MakeWeirdMusic-13)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-americansongwriter.com-15)
texts.4:
As a young child, Vai was influenced by the music his parents had listened to. The album that he cites as his "musical awakening" was the original motion picture soundtrack to the 1961 film _West Side Story_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-16) At age eleven, Vai was introduced to the contemporary rock and progressive music of the era, and after hearing the guitar solo to Led Zeppelin's "Heartbreaker" at age twelve, decided to begin playing the guitar.
In 1973, Vai began to take guitar lessons from fellow New York native Joe Satriani, and played in local bands (the Ohio Express, Circus, and Rayge) throughout his high school years.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-10_Things-17) His friend John Sergio gave him Joe Satriani's number so that Steve and his friend Frankie Munn could get guitar lessons.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-19) In 1978, to further pursue his interest in music composition and theory, Vai attended Berklee College of Music in Boston, Massachusetts after graduating from Carle Place High School.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-20) While at Berklee, Vai began working for Frank Zappa as a transcriptionist, and in the middle of his fourth semester, moved to California to start his career as a session and touring artist for Zappa.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-BerkleePress-21) Also while at Berklee, Vai met his future spouse Pia Maiocco. They have been together since they met and have two children.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-imdbPia-22) In 2003, Vai was awarded an Honorary Doctorate of Music from Berklee.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-23)
texts.5:
### Early music career (1978–1986)
[edit]
Steve Vai (on guitar in between the drums and keyboard, to the right), Frank Zappa and band during a concert at the Memorial Auditorium in Buffalo, New York (October 25, 1980)
In 1978, Vai sent both a notated transcription of Frank Zappa's "The Black Page", and a recording of his college band, Morning Thunder, to Zappa.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-BerkleePress-21)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-VaiVideo-24) Impressed by this, Zappa responded by putting Vai on salary to transcribe his work, which included pieces from the _[Joe's Garage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe's\_Garage "Joe's Garage")_ and _[Shut Up 'n Play Yer Guitar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shut\_Up\_'n\_Play\_Yer\_Guitar "Shut Up 'n Play Yer Guitar")_ albums.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-Tempo_Mental-4) After leaving Berklee College of Music and moving to California, Vai auditioned[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-25) for and became a full-time member of Zappa's band, going on his first tour with Zappa in late 1980.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-BerkleePress-21) Zappa often referred to Vai as his "little Italian virtuoso",[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-26) and Vai is frequently listed in the liner notes of Zappa's albums as having performed "stunt" or "impossible" guitar parts.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-Play_Like_Steve_Vai-27)
texts.6:
### Early music career (1978–1986)
Vai was a featured artist on the 1993 release _[Zappa's Universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zappa's\_Universe "Zappa's Universe")_, and in 2006, Vai appeared as a special guest on Dweezil Zappa's Zappa Plays Zappa tour; both projects won Vai a Grammy Award.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-VaiAwards-28)
After moving on from Zappa's employ in 1983, Vai bought a house in Sylmar, Los Angeles, where he built his first professional studio.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-VaiStudios-29) During this period, Vai formed two bands (The Classified and 777)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-VAI_Bands-6) as well as writing and recording a large amount of music that was not originally intended for release. Out of this material, Vai compiled his first studio album _Flex-Able_. He created his own record label, Akashic Records (later Light Without Heat Records), which he used to take _Flex-Able_ directly to distribution channels.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-30)_Flex-Able_ was released in January 1984.
texts.7:
### Early music career (1978–1986)
Vai began his rise to public acclaim in 1983 when, shortly before the release of _Flex-Able_, his composition "The Attitude Song" was published in _Guitar Player_ magazine.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-Play_Like_Steve_Vai-27) The song centered itself on a main guitar riff in the time signature 7/16, played over a rhythm section centered in 4/4. Each following section of the song showcased a number of specialized techniques (such as two-handed tapping, whammy bar acrobatics, sweep picking, alternate picking, multi-part harmonies, and odd phrasing) used in angular and exaggerated ways that were unique to the song at the time.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-Play_Like_Steve_Vai-27) Interest from the public grew even greater when Vai's song "Blue Powder" (a demonstration for the Carvin X100b amplifier) was published in _Guitar Player_ as well, which showed the virtuoso side of Vai's compositional process. Also in 1986, Vai was cast in the film _Crossroads_ as the Devil's guitar player "Jack Butler". In the famous "duel scene" between Vai and Ralph Macchio's character, Vai wrote and performed all guitar parts with the exception of the slide guitar, which was performed by Ry Cooder.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-31)
In between solo work, Vai replaced Yngwie Malmsteen in June 1984 as the lead guitarist of Alcatrazz, with whom he recorded the album _Disturbing the Peace_. Vai left shortly after the subsequent tour to join David Lee Roth's band.

While I was attending [Berklee College of Music](https://www.facebook.com/BerkleeCollege?__cft__[0]=AZiSYXVnITcak-NXqcgIPsnrNloK2y8ho5uUJJUQmtU6zXXQECJJ0Y_DKxVGffhiY9szQ5WHTXOpf2d6qNxn4s9b5DK_FEMLOkmYgp1ciRarqnWYsztnzVLivjGh5gWdQA8zaK-Zh4P-8BpsrmEi-VcfNSelmXSQSQ&__tn__=-]K-R) in 1978-79, I was in various bands with some outrageously talented young musicians. The first band I formed with my friend Dave Rosenthal was called “Morning Thunder”. Great name for a group ay?
We used to write intense and complex fusion type music with a twist. The band was very bonded and we played with some unbridled youthful chops and insanity.
The band was:
Steve Vai - Guitar
Randy Coven - Bass
Dave Rosenthal - Keyboards
Eddie Rogers - Drums

**Steven Siro Vai**[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-fullname-2) ( _VYE_; born June 6, 1960) is an American guitarist, songwriter, and producer. A three-time Grammy Award winner and fifteen-time nominee,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-tecawards.org-3) Vai started his music career in 1978 at the age of eighteen as a transcriptionist for Frank Zappa,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-Tempo_Mental-4) and played in Zappa's band from 1980 to 1983.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-tecawards.org-3) He embarked on a solo career in 1983 and has released 11 solo albums to date.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-5) He has recorded and toured with Alcatrazz, David Lee Roth, and Whitesnake, as well as recording with artists such as Ozzy Osbourne, Public Image Ltd, Mary J. Blige, Spinal Tap, Alice Cooper, Motörhead, and Polyphia. Additionally, Vai has toured with live-only acts G3, Zappa Plays Zappa, Beat (playing 1980s era King Crimson) and the Experience Hendrix Tour, as well as headlining international tours.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-VAI_Bands-6)

Vai has been described as a "highly individualistic player" and part of a generation of "heavy rock and metal virtuosi who came to the fore in the 1980s".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-7) He released his first solo album _Flex-Able_ in 1984, while his most successful release, _Passion and Warfare_ (1990), was described as "the richest and best hard rock guitar-virtuoso album of the '80s".[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-AllmusicPW-8) He was voted the "10th Greatest Guitarist" by _Guitar World_ magazine's readers,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-guitarworld.com-9) and has sold over 15 million records.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-tecawards.org-3)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-10)
Steve Vai in 2017

Steve Vai, a descendant of Italian immigrants, was born in Carle Place, New York on June 6, 1960. He is the fourth son of John and Theresa Vai.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-11) Vai was raised Roman Catholic.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-12) He described his first experiences with music as, "at the age of five I walked up to [a] piano, hit a note, and noticed that to the right the notes go higher and to the left the notes go lower. In that very moment, I had a full-on epiphany. I was flooded with the instinctual realization of how music was created and how it worked from a theoretical standpoint—the whole language of music was very obvious. I also understood immediately, instinctually, and unequivocally something that has only deepened through the years: that the creation of music is an infinite personal expression. I realized that I could do this, I could make music, and it could be whatever I want."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-http://facebook.com/MakeWeirdMusic-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-americansongwriter.com-15)
It was a year later, at the age of six, that Vai experienced his introduction to the guitar, remembering that, "I saw this nine-year-old boy playing the guitar in my grade school auditorium, and that was another epiphany that I had. It was my first recognition of the instrument. When I saw that guitar and I saw this kid playing it, I knew instinctually that I was going to play the guitar someday, and that it would be my instrument. Don't ask me how I knew, I just knew. It was the coolest thing I had ever seen."[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-http://facebook.com/MakeWeirdMusic-13)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-americansongwriter.com-15)

As a young child, Vai was influenced by the music his parents had listened to. The album that he cites as his "musical awakening" was the original motion picture soundtrack to the 1961 film _West Side Story_.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-16) At age eleven, Vai was introduced to the contemporary rock and progressive music of the era, and after hearing the guitar solo to Led Zeppelin's "Heartbreaker" at age twelve, decided to begin playing the guitar.
In 1973, Vai began to take guitar lessons from fellow New York native Joe Satriani, and played in local bands (the Ohio Express, Circus, and Rayge) throughout his high school years.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-10_Things-17) His friend John Sergio gave him Joe Satriani's number so that Steve and his friend Frankie Munn could get guitar lessons.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-19) In 1978, to further pursue his interest in music composition and theory, Vai attended Berklee College of Music in Boston, Massachusetts after graduating from Carle Place High School.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-20) While at Berklee, Vai began working for Frank Zappa as a transcriptionist, and in the middle of his fourth semester, moved to California to start his career as a session and touring artist for Zappa.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-BerkleePress-21) Also while at Berklee, Vai met his future spouse Pia Maiocco. They have been together since they met and have two children.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-imdbPia-22) In 2003, Vai was awarded an Honorary Doctorate of Music from Berklee.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-23)

### Early music career (1978–1986)
[edit]
Steve Vai (on guitar in between the drums and keyboard, to the right), Frank Zappa and band during a concert at the Memorial Auditorium in Buffalo, New York (October 25, 1980)
In 1978, Vai sent both a notated transcription of Frank Zappa's "The Black Page", and a recording of his college band, Morning Thunder, to Zappa.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-BerkleePress-21)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-VaiVideo-24) Impressed by this, Zappa responded by putting Vai on salary to transcribe his work, which included pieces from the _[Joe's Garage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe's\_Garage "Joe's Garage")_ and _[Shut Up 'n Play Yer Guitar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shut\_Up\_'n\_Play\_Yer\_Guitar "Shut Up 'n Play Yer Guitar")_ albums.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-Tempo_Mental-4) After leaving Berklee College of Music and moving to California, Vai auditioned[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-25) for and became a full-time member of Zappa's band, going on his first tour with Zappa in late 1980.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-BerkleePress-21) Zappa often referred to Vai as his "little Italian virtuoso",[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-26) and Vai is frequently listed in the liner notes of Zappa's albums as having performed "stunt" or "impossible" guitar parts.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-Play_Like_Steve_Vai-27)

### Early music career (1978–1986)
Vai was a featured artist on the 1993 release _[Zappa's Universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zappa's\_Universe "Zappa's Universe")_, and in 2006, Vai appeared as a special guest on Dweezil Zappa's Zappa Plays Zappa tour; both projects won Vai a Grammy Award.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-VaiAwards-28)
After moving on from Zappa's employ in 1983, Vai bought a house in Sylmar, Los Angeles, where he built his first professional studio.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-VaiStudios-29) During this period, Vai formed two bands (The Classified and 777)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-VAI_Bands-6) as well as writing and recording a large amount of music that was not originally intended for release. Out of this material, Vai compiled his first studio album _Flex-Able_. He created his own record label, Akashic Records (later Light Without Heat Records), which he used to take _Flex-Able_ directly to distribution channels.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-30)_Flex-Able_ was released in January 1984.

### Early music career (1978–1986)
Vai began his rise to public acclaim in 1983 when, shortly before the release of _Flex-Able_, his composition "The Attitude Song" was published in _Guitar Player_ magazine.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-Play_Like_Steve_Vai-27) The song centered itself on a main guitar riff in the time signature 7/16, played over a rhythm section centered in 4/4. Each following section of the song showcased a number of specialized techniques (such as two-handed tapping, whammy bar acrobatics, sweep picking, alternate picking, multi-part harmonies, and odd phrasing) used in angular and exaggerated ways that were unique to the song at the time.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-Play_Like_Steve_Vai-27) Interest from the public grew even greater when Vai's song "Blue Powder" (a demonstration for the Carvin X100b amplifier) was published in _Guitar Player_ as well, which showed the virtuoso side of Vai's compositional process. Also in 1986, Vai was cast in the film _Crossroads_ as the Devil's guitar player "Jack Butler". In the famous "duel scene" between Vai and Ralph Macchio's character, Vai wrote and performed all guitar parts with the exception of the slide guitar, which was performed by Ry Cooder.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Vai#cite_note-31)
In between solo work, Vai replaced Yngwie Malmsteen in June 1984 as the lead guitarist of Alcatrazz, with whom he recorded the album _Disturbing the Peace_. Vai left shortly after the subsequent tour to join David Lee Roth's band.

After figuring out the title of her second studio album, Future Nostalgia, Dua Lipa began working backwards, figuring out the sound she desired.[2] Shortly after, "Levitating" was written, which is the first track recorded that appears on the album's final track listing.[3] The song was written by Lipa with her longtime collaborators Clarence Coffee Jr. of The Monsters & Strangerz, Sarah Hudson and Stephen Kozmeniuk, the latter of which also handled the production.[4] Before going into the studio, Kozmeniuk spent a few weeks coming up with ideas to play in the studio, eventually thinking it would be cool to create a "slinky disco track." Lipa sent him some notes and stuff that she was inspired by, which became the idea of blending old with new. Kozmeniuk thought the best way to create this idea was to use old instruments, one of which was a Roland VP-330 synthesizer, which he had been looking for, for seven to eight years. After shipping the synthesizer from Tokyo to Toronto, he immediately plugged it in and began playing. The first thing he played, which he described as a "synthetic choir sound", later turned into the synth line from the song. He looped the sound and began building a song around it, including creating an analog string sound, also using the Roland VP-330.[5]

"Levitating" was written and recorded in a one-day studio session at Sarm West Studios in Notting Hill, London between the four writers on 28 August 2018. They started the session by Hudson doing a Tarot card reading in order for the writers to open up about what was happening in their lives. Lipa recalled it "changing the energy in the room." Kozmeniuk then began playing some tracks he had created with Lipa in mind. "Levitating" was one of the first tracks he played, which the collaborators all agreed that it would be the one to write onto. Lipa took out the voice memos app on her phone and began leading the song by singing a melody, making it up on the way with Coffee later elevating it. They had the visuals of being in an Austin Powers movie, with Mike Myers doing a random dance to the song, which helped give them a mood while writing the lyrics.[5][6][7] The session ended up with the collaborators ordering doughnuts and 'levitating' from the sugar rush.[8][9] They immediately began writing after that, with a good feeling going into it. They decided to include the "sugarboo" lyric as an ode to their friendship as it was something they called one another as a joke.[5] Lipa also decided to add a rap in order to get her British side across, because she often gets mistaken from where she is actually from.[10]

Lipa began by recording the lead vocals, and later some backing vocals and vocals with all the collaborators. They would create different personas with different vocals every time they recorded them. Lipa recalled that she and her co-writers were dancing all through making the song, even if they were experiencing writer's block or working on the production. After finishing the song, Lipa enlisted the help of Stuart Price for some additional production. He brought more "bounce" to the song and helped with the bass groove. He also incorporated a high drone synth as a disco trope, and a string part in the pre-chorus. Koz later also enlisted the help of Bosko "Electrospit" Kante to play a talk box.[5] "Levitating" helped dictate what the rest of Future Nostalgia would sound like and where Lipa thought everything made sense, where she had both the "future" and "nostalgia" elements. She called it the "starting point" of the album.[3][8][9]
Music and lyricsedit

"Levitating" is an electro-disco, nu-disco, pop-funk and space rock song,[11][12][13][14] with dance-pop and power pop elements.[15][16][17] The song incorporates music styles from the 1970s, 1980s, and 1990s pop and R&B.[18][19][20] Constructed in verse–chorus form, the song runs for 3 minutes and 23 seconds and is composed in 4  
4 time and the key of B minor, with a tempo of 103 beats per minute and a chord progression of Bm7—F♯m7—Em7.[10][21][22] It is built around a wonky synth hook, with 1990s choruses and several campy disco tropes.[19][23][24] The rest of the production consists of funky synth disco beats,[25][26] a "squelchy" bass,[19] "rubbery" basslines, syncopated handclaps,[27] nu-disco rhythms,[28] "wonky" and "bizarre" synths,[29][30] an EDM groove,[31] funky guitars, talk box vocals,[32] a "hypnotic" synth line and disco strings.[33] The bass, guitars, and talk box give off a disco-funk feeling. Following the first chorus, the instruments are stripped back.[34] On his remix, DaBaby adds a new pop rap verse and intro, over the original's production,[35][36][37] with him serving as an additional writer on the track.[38]
"Levitating"

Lipa's vocals range from F♯3 to B4.[22] The middle eight includes a Blondie-influenced rap, where Lipa exerts her British accent, before she performs an a cappella ahead of the final chorus.[10][34] "Levitating" has many outer space references,[20][24][39] using an exaggerated metaphor of love as a spaceship to transmit radiant euphoria and happiness.[34][40][41] Lyrically, the song sees Lipa exposing her feelings for a significant other and singing about moments with them in which she is her best self.[34][42] For NME, Rhian Daly stated she sings about "a love 'written in the stars'", while 411Mania's David Hayter, labelled it an "intergalactic ode to orgasms".[43][27] The song received many comparisons to the works of Chic, Daft Punk,[11] Debbie Harry,[44] the Jackson 5 ("Blame It on the Boogie", 1978),[45] Kylie Minogue, Moloko,[46] Kate Nash,[47] Outkast ("Rosa Parks", 1998),[45] Katy Perry,[48] the Spice Girls,[47] Tinie Tempah ("Pass Out", 2010),[43][49] the Weeknd (Starboy, 2016),[17] and Super Mario 64 (1996) sound effects.[33]
It had to be fun and bubbly but with lyrics that felt really smart. This is about me exploring happy songs and doing something that's not 'dance crying'. It's about having fun and meeting someone and falling in love and thinking, 'You've probably met me at the perfect time, let's just go for it.' It's the feeling when love makes you feel like you're levitating. It's otherworldly. Things get quite Daft Punk-y here, but it's playful.
— Lipa on "Levitating".[10]

## Commercial performance
In October 2013, Blacc released the music video for "Wake Me Up". Blacc collaborated with the immigrant rights group National Day Laborer Organizing Network and the ABC* Foundation's Healing Power of Music Initiative. The director is Alex Rivera. The cast were real life immigrant activists: Hareth Andrade Ayala (a Virginia leader in the immigrant youth movement working to stop her own father's deportation), Agustin Chiprez Alvarez (a Los Angeles day laborer), and Margarita Reyes (who was deported with her mother as a child despite being born in the US).[[216]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake_Me_Up_(Avicii_song)#cite_note-216)[[217]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake_Me_Up_(Avicii_song)#cite_note-217)

## Commercial performance
"**Wake Me Up**" was covered in the style of country music in 2013 by the Canadian country singer Tebey featuring the band Emerson Drive.[[230]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake_Me_Up_(Avicii_song)#cite_note-230) This version was released to digital retailers via TebeyMusic on 27 November 2013 as the third single from the former's second studio album, _Two_ (2014) before impacting radio in January 2014.[[231]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake_Me_Up_(Avicii_song)#cite_note-231)[[232]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake_Me_Up_(Avicii_song)#cite_note-232) The song was released in the US on 28 January 2014 through The Talent Associates.[[233]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake_Me_Up_(Avicii_song)#cite_note-tb-233) It was well received by Canadian country radio, peaking at No. 5 on the Canada Country airplay chart. The song is also included on Tebey's 2016 EP, _Old School_.[[234]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake_Me_Up_(Avicii_song)#cite_note-234)

## Commercial performance
### Britton Buchanan and Alicia Keys version
Buchanan and Keys performed the song live on the Season 14 finale of _The Voice_ on 21 May 2018.[[244]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake_Me_Up_(Avicii_song)#cite_note-hl-244) They performed a stripped down rendition of the song and dedicated their performance to Avicii, with Keys saying "This one's for you Avicii! We're celebrating life, love and finding ourselves!".[[240]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake_Me_Up_(Avicii_song)#cite_note-ihr-240)[[244]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake_Me_Up_(Avicii_song)#cite_note-hl-244) Amanda Bell of _Entertainment Weekly_ wrote that "his whimpering tones are a good match for this piece, and her ability to break away is always pretty strong" but concluded that the performance was "still a bit boring".[[245]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake_Me_Up_(Avicii_song)#cite_note-245)

## Commercial performance
### Spark Productions cover
[edit]
In the United Kingdom, the original release date was intended to be 8 September 2013.[[246]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake_Me_Up_(Avicii_song)#cite_note-brandnite-246) In the absence of the original, a group called "Spark Productions" took advantage and released a cover version of it; this version reached number 26 on the UK Singles Chart[[247]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake_Me_Up_(Avicii_song)#cite_note-sparkproductions-247) before Avicii conceded to public demand and decided to release it early, with the Official Charts Company announcing on 15 July 2013 that it would be released that week.[[248]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wake_Me_Up_(Avicii_song)#cite_note-occnr-248)
